response: The implementation of experts' recommendations for follow-up of patients with new cardiovascular implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) in routine clinical practice is not fully adhered to. According to the data, most Medicare beneficiaries who received a new CIED between 2005 and 2009 did not have an initial in-person CIED follow-up visit within 2 to 12 weeks after device implantation. However, the rate of initial follow-up improved over time. Additionally, there is a disparity in follow-up rates among different racial groups, with white patients being more likely to receive follow-up care than patients of other races. This suggests that while there is some improvement in implementing experts' recommendations, there is still a need for increased adherence to guidelines and efforts to address racial disparities in follow-up care.
